note: _cadent in ore gladii_ (Weber/Gryson, Clementina, NVg) – they will fall by the mouth of the sword; no doubt a Hebraism for _cadent acie gladii (acies_ = sharpness) – they will fall by the sharpness of the sword. – Michael Metlen: The Vulgate Gospels as a Translation (continued). _Catholic Biblical Quarterly_ 9 (1947) 106–110, at p. 107.
_virtutes caelorum_ – the powers of heaven = the military forces of heaven; die Heere des Himmels. The word _virtus_ is frequently used in this sense. – Kaulen, p. 34.

_caelum et terram transibunt_ / _verba mea non transient_ (Weber/Gryson) – heaven and earth will perish, but my words shall not perish. The Wordsworth/White edition (see above, Chapter 13.2) has _transibunt_ both times (like the Clementina and the NVg), explaining in a note that this must have been what Jerome in his revision had intended, but carelessly left the second clause untouched.

_in_ (…) _curis huius vitae_ – in the cares of this life. The underlying Greek _mérimna_ is normally rendered _sollicitudo_ in the Vulgate, and not _cura_; cf. Matt 13:22 – _sollicitudo saeculi istius_ – the care of this world. Luke 22–24. For a German working translation with notes on vocabulary and grammar, see Frank Oborski: _Vulgata-Lesebuch. Clavis Vulgatae. Lesestücke aus der lateinischen Bibel mit didaktischer Übersetzung, Anmerkungen und Glossar_. Stuttgart 2022 (343 pp.), pp. 208–232.
